inaccurate.instructions: `index_line` is one line in the index of a repo's agent-instructions file. An agent reads it to decide whether to open the reference doc whose headings and opening paragraph are in `doc`. Does the line misdescribe that doc: does it claim a topic the doc doesn't cover, or leave out a major topic the doc covers, so that an agent looking for that topic wouldn't open this doc? Answer no when the line names the doc's purpose rather than listing its contents, abbreviates its headings, or leaves out minor sections. Answer no for a routing condition in the line ('read it before ...') or a link to another doc: only the line can carry those. A heading whose section only says its content moved elsewhere is not a topic the doc covers.
